items.title: Mikel Arteta defends job cuts at Arsenal to help club ‘evolve and create success’
items.summary: Up to 60 roles at risk after structural review Arteta signed new deal worth more than £20m a season Mikel Arteta has defended Arsenal’s decision to cut up to 60 jobs and insisted it was felt to be necessary to ensure they can continue achieving success. The Premier League champions are understood to have informed the staff whose positions are at risk after a consultation process started by Boston Consulting Group (BCG) before the end of last season. Arsenal hope the number of redundancies can be reduced and will attempt to redeploy affected employees wherever possible, although some job losses may be unavoidable.

items.summary: Javier Tebas accuses Madrid of ‘propaganda techniques’ Club want ‘immediate resignation’ for ‘constant attacks’ Real Madrid have again demanded the resignation of the president of La Liga after he compared the club’s efforts to discredit referees with the propaganda techniques of Nazi Germany. Javier Tebas lashed out at Madrid on Friday on social media with a long post that criticised how its club television channel says referees hurt its chances of winning. The channel regularly runs reels of what it considers gross errors by match officials who are set to work upcoming games for the 15-time European champions.

items.title: ‘It’s really not a drama’: Carrick sticks to the script after Martínez storm
items.summary: Manchester United head coach produced a masterclass in dialling down emotion before a tricky trip to Leeds Michael Carrick returned his most impressive performance precisely when required as he took questions in the midst of the first crisis engulfing him as Manchester United’s manager. His team are bombing in the league after the club’s poorest start since 1986 and out of the Carabao Cup , and after Tuesday’s Champions League defeat at Atlético Madrid Lisandro Martínez showed up ruptures at United by calling out the director of football , Jason Wilcox.

items.title: Carrick brushes off Martínez’s failure to apologise publicly to United director Wilcox

Martínez referred directly to Wilcox after the 2-0 Champions League loss, saying: “I expect more from our technical director.” Continue reading

items.title: Álvaro Arbeloa’s push to make Fulham free-flowing is floundering already
items.summary: Spanish head coach will be under huge pressure if he comes unstuck again at home to Hull on Saturday Fulham fans fretting about life under Álvaro Arbeloa will not feel any better when they remember how things were under Marco Silva, who was one of the most effective managers in the Premier League when it came to making substitutions. Silva’s substitutes were involved in the fourth-highest goal contributions last season and the most in the 2024-25 season. Fulham knew how to dig in and salvage unlikely points.

items.title: Hong Kong club hope David Silva can be their hero – but just for one day
items.summary: Former Manchester City player is coming out of retirement at 40 to play one match for ambitious Supreme Sha Tin Hong Kong, China (as is the official football name), has long tried to follow the advice of Han Solo in Return of the Jedi: keeping their distance from China while trying not to look like they are keeping their distance. It is all about maintaining an independent football association and the trappings and privilege that come with it. There was some talk a few years ago about getting a Hong Kong team in the Chinese Super League, when the spending was in full flow, and although that did not happen the local Premier League has belatedly got in on the act – kind of.

items.title: Wolves extend Burnley’s home woes to a full year as Vardy strikes in vain
items.summary: The Wolves substitute Tawanda Chirewa struck within seconds of coming off the bench as César Peixoto’s side came from behind to extend Burnley’s home misery at Turf Moor to 21 games without a win. Chirewa had just replaced Sean Neave in the 72nd minute when Mateus Mané pounced on Igor Julio’s heavy touch and sent the 23-year-old Zimbabwe international through to strike an angled shot, which flew into the net despite Grégoire Coudert getting his hands to the effort.

items.title: The Florian Wirtz mystery: why has he not found Leverkusen form at Liverpool?
items.summary: Two of our writers pick over the German’s contribution to Liverpool and what the £116m forward could yet produce Some criticism has been OTT and a fee rising to £116m heightens demands but, yes, compared with his performances in Germany and for Germany Wirtz has underwhelmed at Liverpool. The past week has encapsulated his Liverpool career so far. In the Champions League rout of Lask he was everywhere, exploiting gaps between and behind the Austrian club’s defence and knitting together a dominant display against limited opposition.
